Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a category.
Let $p : \mathcal{S} \to \mathcal{C}$ be a category over $\mathcal{C}$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The composition of two strongly cartesian morphisms
is strongly cartesian.
\item Any isomorphism of $\mathcal{S}$ is strongly cartesian.
\item Any strongly cartesian morphism $\varphi$ such that $p(\varphi)$
is an isomorphism, is an isomorphism.
\end{enumerate}

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a category.
Let $p : \mathcal{S} \to \mathcal{C}$ be a category over $\mathcal{C}$.
Let $x \to y$ and $z \to y$ be morphisms of $\mathcal{S}$.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $x \to y$ is strongly cartesian,
\item $p(x) \times_{p(y)} p(z)$ exists, and
\item there exists a strongly cartesian morphism $a : w \to z$ in
$\mathcal{S}$ with $p(w) = p(x) \times_{p(y)} p(z)$ and
$p(a) = \text{pr}_2 : p(x) \times_{p(y)} p(z) \to p(z)$.
\end{enumerate}
Then the fibre product $x \times_y z$ exists and is isomorphic to $w$.

Let $\mathcal{S}_1$, $\mathcal{S}_2$ be categories over $\mathcal{C}$.

as categories over $\mathcal{C}$.
Then $\mathcal{S}_1$ is fibred over $\mathcal{C}$ if and only if
$\mathcal{S}_2$ is fibred over $\mathcal{C}$.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a category and let $F:\mathcal X\to\mathcal S$ and $G:\mathcal Y\to\mathcal S$ be $1$-morphisms of fibred categories over $\mathcal C$. Their $2$-fibre product exists in the $(2,1)$-category of fibred categories over $\mathcal C$. One explicit model has objects $(U,x,y,\alpha)$, where $U\in\Ob(\mathcal C)$, $x\in\mathcal X_U$, $y\in\mathcal Y_U$, and $\alpha:F(x)\xrightarrow{\sim}G(y)$ is an isomorphism in $\mathcal S_U$. Its morphisms are pairs $(a:x\to x', b:y\to y')$ over the same arrow $U\to U'$ satisfying $G(b)\circ\alpha=\alpha'\circ F(a)$. The resulting category belongs to fibred categories over $\mathcal C$, and the obvious projections and comparison isomorphism exhibit the stated $2$-fibre product.
